column1: # CLASSIFICATION -- what KIND of change this is, and therefore which rules apply.
# RETAINED BUT NOT EXERCISED. 004 is about the environment/host distinction,
# and it uses no pull requests, no workflow and no validation. itil:* is here
# because it has to FIT the structure, not because this repo tests it. Any
# claim 004 makes about it is [H].
# IT IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF THING FROM THE OTHER THREE, and that is why it gets
# its own file rather than a column in manifest.tsv:
#     app:core     what moves          )
#     APP_HOST     where it is placed  ) three facts about a RUNNING PROGRAM
#     RAILS_ENV    how it behaves      )
#     itil:*       which rules apply   -- a fact about a PROPOSAL to change it
# The first three are observable by asking the estate; you can curl for them.
# The fourth cannot be observed at all -- there is nothing to measure, because
# it is a judgement made before the change exists in any environment. A guard
# that tries to derive it from the diff is deriving blast radius and calling it
# risk, which is a different question wearing the same word.
# One and only one applies to any change. That exclusivity is the rule; nothing
# in 004 enforces it, and a later build that does should be able to show it
# refusing two.
# label
itil:standard
column2: pre-authorised, routine, the change type this pipeline exists to make boring
column3: none needed; the classification IS the authorization

column1: itil:normal
itil:emergency
column2: the remedy for something already wrong
column3: a person, and recorded retrospectively -- ITIL 4 documents an emergency AFTER, it does not skip the record
